author: dgusakov
content:
Dear CL developers,

Lido contributors, including myself, have proposed 2 EIPs for Hegota:
- https://forkcast.org/eips/8148/
- https://forkcast.org/eips/8205/
Since you all are tasked with creating Hegota ratings by mid-Sept, I want to share a short TL;DR on both EIPs to make it easier for you to rate them.

author: dgusakov
content:
**EIP-8148: Custom sweep threshold for validators**

This EIP solves an issue that we have had since Pectra. We have only 2 validator size options: 32 ETH (`0x01`) and 2048 ETH (`0x02`). While the initial assumption was that compounding `0x02` validators would be considered to have a dynamic size, this was never recognised by the community or stakers.

What is proposed is to make an `0x02` validator size configurable. It is done via the introduction of the additional validator property - sweep threshold. Managed via EIP-7685 from EL, this parameter is adjustable and can also be specified when creating a validator.

This EIP solves several more issues:
- There will be no more excuses for anyone with more than 1 `0x01` validator to reject consolidation to `0x02`.
- We will get the unique opportunity to change or remove `MAX_EB` in the future. All current validators will have an opt-in path to increase their sweep threshold and choose the new size that fits them best. No new WC type. No migration.

author: dgusakov
content:
**EIP-8205: Withdrawal credentials preregistration**

This EIP solves a long-standing vulnerability in the Ethereum validator deposit process (https://ethresear.ch/t/deposit-contract-exploit/6528) by introducing a way for the validators to bind their public key to a WC address before making any deposit.

While some of you might say that this is an application-layer issue, we all should admit that this issue originates from the way we designed the deposit process back in the day. A detailed analysis shows how painful it is for the application layer to deal with the issue and the scale of the issue - https://hackmd.io/@george-avs/r1oK_afsbe.

If implemented, this EIP would reduce the pressure staking protocols and operators are facing, especially during hard forks when the prevention tooling and approaches should be updated. Without this pressure, the application layer can focus on more important stuff for Ethereum like speeding up consolidation process, improving decentralization, and (I'm shocked I'm saying it) maybe even be more open to the issuance reduction. All because they will have less routine work to do and lower costs.

author: dgusakov
content:
I hope this summary will help you understand why we believe these EIPs should be in Hegota and will help you with ranking them. I'm always here with the rest of the Lido team to answer your questions and have open discussions.

Have a great day, and let's keep Ethereum great together!
